title: Implement staged cache warmup + hysteresis thresholds and one-click rollback playbook for Optimize recommendations
creator: Leah Martinez
description:
Summary:
A production incident on 2025-02-08 caused a cascade of dropped cache hits and aggressive batch resizing after an automated Optimize recommendation was applied. The root cause was an immediate global apply of a lowered cache TTL + higher batch-size suggestion without a staged warmup or hysteresis window; the system overcompensated and exceeded tail-latency SLOs for high-priority tenants.

Objective:
Deliver a combined engineering and operations solution that: (1) prevents rapid destabilization when Optimize pushes config changes, (2) provides deterministic safe-apply semantics (dry-run metrics, shadow warmup), and (3) enables an operator-triggered, fast rollback/mitigation path from Console and CLI. Produce a runnable playbook for on-call and SRE teams.

Proposed mitigations and design decisions:
- Staged Warmup (shadow mirror): new recommendation applies initially in "shadow" mode for a configurable window (default 30m) where a % of traffic is mirrored to the new config and warm caches are populated without affecting production responses. Mirror sampling should be per-tenant and rate-limited.
- Hysteresis thresholds: require a three-point confirmation (delta thresholds for cache-hit-rate, median latency, 99.9th latency) before a full global promote. Default: cache-hit-rate increase >= 1.5x OR cost reduction >= 8% without latency regression > 5% at p99.
- Transactional apply with dry-run metrics: introduce an apply transaction ID and dry-run phase that emits simulated cost/latency projections and stores metrics to a temporary namespace for review. Dry-run must complete in <15m for configs affecting <= 100 tenants.
- Auto-revert TTL: if the promoted config causes p99 latency regression > 15% for >5 minutes, auto-revert the config and create an incident ticket. Revert must be idempotent and annotated in audit log.
- Operator tools: Console one-click rollback and CLI (redwood-optimize rollback <txn>) that cross-checks the transaction and performs safe revert with diagnostics. Include a Canary toggle in Console per-tenant.
- Metrics & visibility: extend optimizer dashboards with transaction-level timelines, dry-run vs promoted comparisons, and a synthetic prompt suite to surface output-quality regressions.

Acceptance criteria:
- Staged warmup implemented and enabled behind a feature flag in optimize-service; demo showing mirror population for a synthetic tenant.
- Hysteresis guardrails enforced for all automated recommendations; unit and integration tests covering threshold permutations.
- Dry-run phase exposes projected cost and latency delta in Console within 10m of apply start.
- CLI rollback and Console rollback validated in a runbook drill.
- Playbook checked into Confluence and a runbook drill executed with SRE and on-call signoffs.

Risks / tradeoffs:
- Slower time-to-realize savings due to staged application; acceptable to prioritize safety.
- Increased complexity in optimizer service; we'll mitigate with clear observability and strong test coverage.

Delivery plan:
Week 1 (2025-02-10 -> 2025-02-16): design and API for transactional apply, proto dry-run metrics, and feature flag.
Week 2 (2025-02-17 -> 2025-02-23): implement mirror warmup pipeline, add hysteresis evaluator, basic Console hooks.
Week 3 (2025-02-24 -> 2025-03-02): integration testing, runbook drill, CLI rollback, and SRE signoff.
